status: V3 development boundary labels; synthetic cases, not observed model results or a production accuracy estimate.
safety: Invented text only. This file is evaluator data: send only input, never labels, rationale or case identifiers. This is separate from the original 20-note trial and independent held-out sets.
limits: These examples encode the intended scope. Offline fixture checks validate transport/schema/lifecycle, not classification. Evaluate a frozen prompt on independently held-out cases before activation.

input.title: Counterexample to the lower bound
input.body: The claimed lower bound is false at n=1.

cases.rationale: One relevant observation is enough; no length or proof-completeness gate.

input.title: Reaction to the lower bound
input.body: This fucking bound is a steaming pile of shit. Fuck this proof and fuck this whole garbage result. It is worthless fucking trash.

cases.rationale: A profanity-heavy degrading attack on the result can warrant human attention without a personal target.

input.title: The implementation is badly designed
input.body: This implementation is badly designed: it performs a cubic inversion for every ciphertext. That is an avoidable cost. The authors need to fix it.

cases.rationale: Direct negative criticism of work and a request to its authors are not personal degradation.

input.title: Repeated matrix inversion
input.body: Caching the inverse would reduce setup work. Anyone who wrote this is a pathetic idiot and should shut up.

cases.rationale: A substantive point does not erase gratuitous personal degradation; the suggested correction should retain the point.

input.title: A missing carry in my code
input.claim: A missing carry in my code
input.body: Damn, I forgot the carry. Correcting that changes my test vector, and the failure disappears.

cases.rationale: An incidental expletive alongside an identifiable technical observation is allowed.
The entire post is an isolated outburst without an identifiable contribution; no serious-harm claim is needed.

input.title: Correctness question
input.body: Does this error distribution still give the same decryption-failure bound?

cases.rationale: A short research question is a legitimate contribution.
There is no question, observation, reference or task context to publish.

input.title: A monoid-action idea
input.body: Could a noninvertible monoid action hide a trapdoor? I do not know a reduction or even whether the construction can decrypt yet.

cases.rationale: Exploratory mathematical questions do not require a known connection or correctness evidence to pass publication screening.

input.title: Weekend furniture sale
input.body: Buy my sofa and dining table. Collection before Saturday. Message me for prices.

cases.rationale: The standalone sales post has no research or relevant collaboration context.

input.title: Review tone incident
input.body: The response to my decoding note was: "Your fucking decoder is worthless shit." I am quoting the wording so moderators can examine the exchange; my technical question remains whether the retry bound is valid.

cases.rationale: A hostile quotation reported as evidence is not endorsement.

input.title: Decoder retry bound
input.body: The expected retry count is 1/(1-p). This fucking garbage decoder is utter shit, the whole approach is fucking worthless trash, and no one should waste time discussing this shit.

cases.rationale: On-topic mathematical content does not excuse a dominant profane tirade.

input.title: Crucible estimates are misleading
input.body: Crucible is presenting a misleading comparison: setup costs are excluded from one curve and included in another. That reporting choice is unacceptable and should be corrected.

cases.rationale: Criticism of the platform, including strongly negative judgment, remains allowed.

input.title: An unproved factoring shortcut
input.body: Conjecture: every odd composite is divisible by seven. I have not checked examples and would welcome counterexamples.

cases.rationale: An obviously wrong or weak mathematical claim is still outside the abuse/relevance decision.

input.title: A paper on syndrome decoding
input.body: Reference: Example and Sample, Synthetic notes on syndrome decoding, example.invalid/synthetic-decoding. The lower-bound discussion may be relevant to our code-based stages.

cases.rationale: A short literature pointer is sufficient without fetching or certifying the paper.

input.title: Reading group on code-based KEMs
input.body: Could someone join a reading session on the decoding reduction next Thursday? I am especially stuck on the reduction loss.

cases.rationale: Relevant coordination is not unrelated chatter.

input.title: A finite combinatorics observation
input.body: For the first few n I found that each path has an even number of turns. I have no proof, and I do not know whether this has any cryptographic use.

cases.rationale: An uncertain contribution to mathematics is not spam just because an application is unknown.
